title: Initialize and Print a Static Array
description: Declare an integer array named `numbers` of a fixed size of 5. Initialize this array directly during its declaration with the values: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. After initialization, use a `for` loop to print each element in the format: 'Array element at index X: Y' where X is the index and Y is the value.
constraints: Array size is fixed at 5. Elements are fixed as specified. Use a `for` loop to iterate and print.
sample_output:
Array element at index 0: 10
Array element at index 1: 20
Array element at index 2: 30
Array element at index 3: 40
Array element at index 4: 50
explanation: The output lists each array element and its index using a for loop.

title: Accessing Specific Array Elements
description: Write a C program that declares a character array (which is a C-style string) named `programName` and initialize it with the value "C-Program". Your task is to access and print the following: the first character, the third character, and the last character (not the null terminator).
constraints: The string 'C-Program' has a fixed length. Correctly identify the index for the last character (remembering null termination).
sample_output:
First character: C
Third character: P
Last character: m
explanation: The output shows the first, third, and last character of the string 'C-Program'.

title: Calculate Sum of Array Elements from User Input
description: Write a C program that prompts the user to enter 5 integer values. Store these 5 integers into an array. After all inputs are received, calculate the sum of all the elements stored in the array and print the result.
constraints: Array size is fixed at 5. Input integers will be between -100 and 100. Use a loop for input and another loop for summation.
sample_output: The sum of all array elements is: 150
explanation: The numbers are stored in an array and their sum is printed.

title: Find Maximum Element in an Array
description: Develop a C program that reads 5 integer values from the user and stores them in an array. Once the array is populated, your program should traverse the array to find the single largest (maximum) value and print it.
constraints: Array size is fixed at 5. Input integers will be between -1000 and 1000. Use a loop to find the maximum.
sample_output: The maximum element in the array is: 90
explanation: The largest of the entered numbers (90) is determined and printed.

title: Reverse Array Elements In-Place
description: Write a C program that reads 5 integers into an array from the user. After reading, modify the array in-place so that its elements are in reverse order. Print both the original and reversed arrays.
constraints: Array size is fixed at 5. Input integers will be between 1 and 100. Reverse in-place (no auxiliary array). Print space-separated on one line.
explanation: The original array is printed, then its elements are reversed and printed.

title: Search for an Element in an Array
description: Create a C program that first prompts the user to enter 10 integer values to populate an array. After the array is filled, ask the user to enter a single `search_key` integer. Search for this key in the array using linear search. If found, print the index; otherwise, print not found.
constraints: Array size is 10. All integers (array elements and search key) will be between 0 and 100. Implement a linear search.
explanation: The number 70 is found at index 6 of the array.

title: Count Frequency of Each Element in an Array
description: Write a C program that reads 10 integers into an array from the user. Assume that these input integers will be within the range of 1 to 10 (inclusive). Your task is to count how many times each number occurs and print the frequency for each present value.
constraints: Array size is 10. Input elements are guaranteed to be integers between 1 and 10. Use an auxiliary array for counting.
sample_output:
Frequency of elements:
1 appears 3 times
2 appears 3 times
3 appears 2 times
4 appears 1 time
5 appears 1 time
explanation: The frequency of each number present in the array is printed.

title: Matrix Addition (2x2 Two-Dimensional Arrays)
description: Write a C program that performs matrix addition for two 2x2 integer matrices. Prompt the user to enter the elements for the first matrix row by row, then do the same for the second matrix. Print the resulting matrix after addition.
constraints: Both matrices are fixed 2x2. Matrix elements will be integers between -100 and 100. Use nested loops for input and calculation.
explanation: The corresponding elements of the two matrices are summed and printed.

title: Demonstrating Array Out-of-Bounds Access (Undefined Behavior)
description: Write a C program that declares a small integer array, for example, `int arr[5];`. Then, deliberately attempt to write a value to an index that is outside the bounds of this array (e.g., arr[10] = 99;). Observe and explain the result.
constraints: The array size is small and fixed. The out-of-bounds access should be clearly demonstrable.
sample_output: The program may terminate abnormally with a runtime error such as 'Segmentation fault' or 'Bus error'.
explanation: Accessing out-of-bounds memory causes undefined behavior in C, such as a segmentation fault.

title: Student Exam Score Analysis (2D Array)
description: Imagine you are developing a system to analyze student performance. You have 5 students, and each student has scores for 3 subjects. This data can be naturally represented using a two-dimensional array. Read the scores, print the total for each student, and then calculate the average for each subject.
constraints: Number of students is 5, number of subjects is 3. Scores are integers between 0 and 100. Assume valid numerical input. Use nested loops for input and calculations.
sample_output:
--- Student Totals ---
Student 1 Total: 240
Student 2 Total: 210
Student 3 Total: 270
Student 4 Total: 225
Student 5 Total: 180

--- Subject Averages ---
Subject 1 Average: 71.00
Subject 2 Average: 74.00
Subject 3 Average: 80.00
explanation: Each student's total is calculated, and then each subject's average across all students is printed.
